category_title: English language learners who struggle to comprehend abstract literary nuances without visual aids
student_description: Jasmine is an English language learner who is highly reluctant and shy when asked to analyze print-only text, often providing vague or confused answers. However, she demonstrates strong analytical and predictive skills when literary and historical concepts are anchored in visual media (like films) and when she is allowed to express her understanding through creative, multimodal projects.

criteria.rationale: Jasmine struggles to infer or predict from print text alone but excels when drawing connections to visual media like films.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly references, introduces, or asks the student to recall a visual element (e.g., a film scene, an image, or a cinematic comparison) to help her analyze, infer, or predict.

criteria.rationale: Abstract moral dilemmas or print-based visualization exercises cause Jasmine to withdraw, whereas asking about her emotional reactions to scenes stimulates her engagement.
criteria.check: The tutor asks the student to describe her feelings, emotional reactions, or sensory observations regarding a scene or character, rather than asking for purely factual or abstract literary definitions.

criteria.rationale: Jasmine benefits from structured formats to translate what she sees in visual media into complex literary concepts.
criteria.check: The tutor provides or suggests a structured tool (such as a graphic organizer, chart, or guided note-taking format) to help the student connect visual or cinematic elements to literary themes.
